A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain readable main sections and appendices A–G. Their text, equations, figures and tables support a reliable comparison despite page reflow.

before.justification: V3 reports original simulations using reconstructed EU ETS auction data in Sections 5.3 and 6.2, with data-analysis and simulation details in Appendix F.

after.justification: V4 retains these original simulations and data analyses, including Figure 4, Figure 5, Table 2 and Appendix F.

M1.justification: The safe-strategy construction, DAG representation, edge estimators and Algorithms 1–5 retain their procedures. The revisions concern parameter tuning and clarification of existing unknown-horizon handling, without introducing a new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate richness ratios and sliding-window RoI strategies using the same reconstructed 2022–2023 EU ETS auction data and synthetic valuations. No evaluated dataset, domain or scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Figures 4–5 retain the same comparisons: safe strategies against feasible-strategy value bounds, one-pair against more expressive safe strategies, and shifted strategies against per-round safe strategies.

E3.justification: The simulation protocols remain unchanged: Appendix F retains T sampled from 100–300, M from 10–80 and m from 1–10; Section 6.2 retains T = 200 and the same RoI windows, metrics and controls.

E4.justification: The analyses of richness versus bid complexity and cumulative value versus per-round feasibility are retained. No ablation, robustness test, sensitivity analysis or case study is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report 100 simulations for Figure 4, 50 for the Section 6.2 experiments, standard-deviation shading in Figure 4 and the same feasibility box plots.

E6.justification: The empirical plots, Table 2 entries and reported findings are unchanged. For example, Table 2 retains a violation fraction of 0.3225 and median relative feasibility of 0.0231 for T0 = 8; Figure 4 retains richness exceeding 0.95 for m ≥ 4.

T1.justification: Appendix B.3 corrects the squared-edge-weight bound from O(mM^3) to O(mM^4), substantially revising a principal guarantee: Theorem 4.4 changes bandit regret from O(M^(3/2)m^(3/2)sqrt(T log M)) to O(M^2 m^(3/2)sqrt(T log M)). Claim B.1's induction hypothesis is also amended, and Appendix E.6 explains how unknown context counts are handled in the regret argument.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution summary weaken the claimed bandit regret dependence on M from M^(3/2) to M^2. The central claims about safe strategies, efficient learning, richness ratios and extensions otherwise retain their scope.

C2.justification: V4 removes the Appendix B.3 assertion that normalized bandit regret has sublinear dependence on M. Appendix E.6 corrects the stochastic benchmark's information description to competing bids plus the context distribution, consistent with the existing model, and stops describing the adversarial-context lower bound as matching.

D1.justification: Appendix B.3 changes the prescribed bandit learning rate from M^(-1)sqrt(log M/(mMT)) to M^(-2)sqrt(log M/(mT)). Appendix E.6 explicitly explains using the doubling trick for unknown per-context horizons. Data reconstruction and access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V4 adds Burkett and Woodward (2020) to support last-accepted-bid pricing and removes Zhang et al. (2024), previously cited in the deleted normalized-regret footnote. The broader research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: There are limited prose, footnote and reference edits without substantial narrative restructuring. V4 incorrectly changes many cross-reference labels to Theorem while retaining statement labels such as Lemma, Claim and Assumption, including Assumption 6.4.

P2.justification: V4 places Figure 3 before Theorem 4.2 and Figure 5 before Table 2, with associated page reflow. The figures and tables retain their substantive displays, axes, legends and captions.

improvement.justification: V4 repairs an incorrect edge-weight estimate and aligns the bandit guarantee and learning-rate prescription with the corrected analysis. The contextual clarifications also improve precision. Newly incorrect theorem cross-references reduce clarity, but the mathematical corrections provide a limited net improvement while the framework and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
